commentarial_sequence: पिप्पली। हरीतकी। कोशातकी। शमी। करीरी। पृथिवी। क्रोष्ट्री।

first_members.sense: feminine named by the commentary; botanical identification unassigned

compound_controls.decision: Nyāsa: the listed feminine prevents restoration of a masculine first member. Padamañjarī asks whether this earth-word can satisfy the ordinary same-ground condition in the first place.
The same descriptive ground applies to either gender; the co-referential feminine first member takes masculine-like shape.
The first member lacks the requisite masculine use on the same ground.
The prescribed ūṅ in the first member excludes the masculine-like replacement.

literal_spans_in_whitespace_joined_entry: of a plant and of its fruit

scope: The Nyāsa assigns the local presentation of examples to the author of the vṛtti; neither the seven tokens nor the separately printed compound examples assert a closed pippalyādi membership.
The Bālamanoramā explains the need to list pippalī even though it denotes a class: its fixed feminine gender matters. It asks the purpose of pippalyādi as an internal sublist.

At 6.3.34 the masculine must be used on the same ground of application, the following feminine must be co-referential and not an excluded member, and the first must lack ūṅ. The final shortening of subordinate bhāryā (1.2.48) is independent of the first-member decision.

The inflection archive assigns the kroṣṭrī head a plant gloss. Its letter forms serve as a formal comparison; the female jackal meaning here has an independent dictionary and grammatical witness. The distinct plant sense earns no second table.
An entire seven-name compound series has no local source: only the four explicitly printed masculine possessive examples are declined.
